S1_incident_reporting.quote: An initial report is due within 72 hours of learning of the incident, followed by a complete investigation report within 30 days. Customers whose unit was involved must be notified within 5 business days, with known hazards and immediate safety steps; material updates must be sent as they become available.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: The maximum allowed failure rate is 5% per model. A model exceeding 5% is non-compliant; the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and submit a corrective-action plan. The regulator shall set proportionate safeguards and a retesting timeline based on risk; sales may continue subject to those safeguards unless the regulator determines a pause is necessary. Full per-model results, including failure rates, must be provided confidentially to the regulator. Customers must receive safety notices describing known hazards and recommended protective actions, but not individual-company per-model failure rates.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New battery systems must provide a remote emergency shut-off capability. Manufacturers must enable the capability on compatible installed units and provide a safe retrofit or replacement plan for units that lack it, completing the program within 6 years of adoption.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: Built-in fire suppression is required on new battery systems manufactured 36 months or more after adoption.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: Full model-specific thermal-test results, including failure rates, must be provided confidentially to the regulator; customer notices must not publish individual-company per-model failure rates. A model exceeding 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period triggers prompt regulator notification and a regulator-led risk review, initiated within 30 days. The regulator must require a recall when the review determines that the model presents an unacceptable risk.

document.section_notes: S1 requires all incidents reported within 72 hours and customer notice within 5 business days. S2 sets a 5% test limit but allows continued sales under regulator safeguards and keeps per-model results confidential from customers, violating Halcyon's red line. S3 sets a 6-year retrofit deadline and S4 a 36-month suppression deadline; S5 uses an 8/100k review trigger with recall only if the regulator finds unacceptable risk.
